other_failure_modes.name: Temporal leakage in test set lag features
other_failure_modes.description: When computing lag features (e.g., `shift(1)`) on the test set in isolation, the first few rows result in NaNs. By using backward fill (`bfill()`) to handle these, future test data is leaked into the predictions for earlier time steps. To prevent this, the end of the training sequence should be concatenated with the test sequence prior to calculating lags.
other_failure_modes.evidence:
test_feat = add_sequence_lags(test_feat)
... 
df_all[f"{col}_lag1"] = df_all[col].shift(1)
... 
df_all = df_all.bfill().ffill()

other_failure_modes.name: Overfitting ensemble weights to validation set
other_failure_modes.description: The agent optimizes the ensemble blending weights using the validation set predictions and ground truth, and then reports the final performance score on this exact same validation set. This results in an overly optimistic evaluation score due to data leakage.

summary: The agent submitted a highly sophisticated solution featuring excellent domain-specific feature engineering (psychrometrics), deep learning, and gradient boosting models. However, it suffers from temporal leakage in the test set because lag features are computed on the test set in isolation and missing initial values are backward-filled. Additionally, the final validation score reported is overly optimistic because the ensemble blending weights were tuned on the exact same validation set.
